title: Friendship (III.17–III.22)
hookLine: scroll back through your messages with one friend: is it a help desk, or something shared?
tomorrow: the team chat is roasting Valeria. Sofia's typing. what now?

cards: Scroll back through your messages with one close friend. How many start with "can I ask you something"? How many with "saw this and thought of you"?
Some friendships slowly turn into a help desk: one side brings problems, the other fixes them. Francis de Sales says you can tell what a friendship is by what passes between the two people in it.

teach.h: CHARITY FOR ALL, FRIENDSHIP FOR SOME.
teach.b: So, the question: what makes a friendship true? First, the wide circle. Love everyone, Francis says, with the love of charity.
Friendship is narrower: a love that is shared, given and returned, and it can't be with everyone.
Second, what passes between. If what two friends share is empty, flattery, looks, idle charm, the friendship is empty too.
If they share what is good, honesty, knowledge, kindness, faith, it's true, and he calls it precious. Third, a warning in a jar.
He tells of a honey from Heraclea that looks like any other honey and is poison. False friendship is like that: sweet words, fond looks, same color, same shine.

The book Catholics call Ecclesiasticus says it in the Douay-Rheims: "A faithful friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found him, hath found a treasure." A neighbor tradition says something close.
In a Buddhist sutta, the Buddha's companion Ananda says that admirable friendship is half of the holy life. The Buddha answers: not half.

teach.h: THE WHOLE OF THE HOLY LIFE.
teach.b: It is the whole of the holy life. The shared ground: a good friend isn't an extra on the spiritual road; it sits near the center.

And one honest difference. The Buddha means a friend who helps you walk the noble eightfold path he taught. Francis means a friendship that shares charity, the love of God as Christians understand it.
Two traditions, each in its own words, and neither one treats a friend as small.

how: Some Catholics meet with a friend or small group to pray, read Scripture or talk honestly about their lives of faith.

o: a promise to agree with someone no matter what
the love a person owes to every stranger
a love shared and returned between two people

p: is a good friend half the holy life?

s: in the sutta, the Buddha agrees that admirable friendship is half of the holy life
Ananda says half. the Buddha answers: not half, the whole of it.
Francis says to love everyone, but friendship can't be with everyone
charity is for all; friendship is a love shared and returned.
Francis asks devout people to give up close friendships
he calls true friendship precious; he warns only against the kind that flatters.

games.q: a new coworker praises everything you do, loudly, every day. an old friend sometimes tells you hard truths, kindly. by Francis's chapter, which friendship looks truer?
o: the old friend, who shares honesty and good things.
the coworker, because the words are kinder.
neither; friends should stay out of your business.
games.why: a friendship is as true as what passes between you. flattery is the honey of Heraclea: same shine, wrong honey.

practice: Think of one friend who has shared something good with you: honesty, a laugh, faith, a hard truth said kindly. Through the sit, write them a one-line thank-you for something specific. Whether you send it is yours to choose.

wordCard.voice: Friendship. For Francis, a love given and returned, as true as the good things that pass between two people.

orig.note: Latin for friendship. Francis de Sales wrote in French, where the word is amitié.

carryVoice: Keep this one: true friends, who share the honey that isn't poison. See you tomorrow.
